dish_name_en: Pike boudin Richelieu with Nantua sauce
dish_name_fr: Boudin de brochet Richelieu, sauce Nantua
note_en: André Pic's own version of the Lyon pike quenelle, rolled into a sausage instead of being shaped with two spoons and served under Nantua sauce.
note_fr: La version d'André Pic de la quenelle lyonnaise, roulée en boudin au lieu d'être tournée à la cuillère et servie sous une sauce Nantua.
why_en: The lean pike proteins bind with egg and cream and set firm as they poach, while the crayfish butter in the Nantua sauce carries the shells' fat-soluble pigments and aromas into the béchamel, which water-based cooking would leave behind.
why_fr: Les protéines maigres du brochet, liées à l'œuf et à la crème, coagulent à la pochée en une masse ferme, tandis que le beurre d'écrevisse de la sauce Nantua transporte dans la béchamel les pigments et arômes liposolubles des carapaces, que l'eau seule n'extrait pas.
source_quote: Entre autres recettes légendaires, il légua à la postérité son interprétation personnelle de la quenelle lyonnaise : le boudin de brochet Richelieu nappé de sauce Nantua, une béchamel additionnée de crème et de beurre d'écrevisse.

audit.problem: Quote is verbatim on the page, in the section headed "Le boudin Richelieu, sauce écrevisses d'André Pic", and explicitly says he bequeathed his personal interpretation of the Lyon quenelle. Only slack: "eggs" in the ingredient list is not in the source (the page names only the Nantua sauce's béchamel, cream and crayfish butter), and note_en's "shaped with two spoons" detail is the auditor's gloss, not the page's. No superlative in note_en; year is "—".
audit.correction: Either drop "eggs" from ingredients or source the panade/egg binding to a quenelle recipe rather than to this page.

dish_name_fr: Poularde à la vapeur
note_en: A Bresse hen studded with truffle and cooked in the steam above a pot of beef, veal and poultry stock rather than simmered in it.
note_fr: Une poularde de Bresse truffée, cuite dans la vapeur au-dessus d'une marmite de bouillons de bœuf, de veau et de volaille, et non pochée dedans.
why_en: Held above the liquid, the bird loses none of its soluble juices to the stock, and the saturated steam holds the flesh at 100 °C without agitation, while the truffle slid under the skin gives its fat-soluble aroma to the subcutaneous fat as that fat melts.
why_fr: Maintenue au-dessus du liquide, la volaille ne cède pas ses sucs solubles au bouillon, et la vapeur saturée la porte à 100 °C sans agitation, pendant que la truffe glissée sous la peau diffuse ses arômes liposolubles dans la graisse sous-cutanée qui fond.
source_quote: Bref, les plus illustres représentants de tous les arts se sont attablés à la Côte-d'Or, pour savourer la timbale de brochet éminence, la terrine de bécasse chaude au chambertin, la poularde à la vapeur, le gâteau du prélat, etc.

audit.problem: Quote is verbatim, but it is a guest-list sentence: "poularde à la vapeur" appears only as one item in a list of what famous diners came to eat at the Côte-d'Or. The page carries NO cooking method, no truffle, no Madeira, no beef or veal stock — so the entire note_en, why_en and four of five ingredients rest on nothing in the cited source. The page's own recipe list later names only "timbale de brochet éminence" and "terrine de bécasse chaude au chambertin" from Dumaine's book "Ma Cuisine" (1972).
audit.correction: Keep the dish but re-source the method to Dumaine's "Ma Cuisine" or a text that actually describes the steam-over-stock cooking; until then strip Madeira, beef stock and veal stock from ingredients and cut why_en's specifics to what a source carries.

dish_name_fr: Gratin de queues d'écrevisses
note_en: Shelled crayfish tails bound in a cream sauce built on crayfish butter and browned in the dish, kept on the Auberge du Père Bise menu by later chefs.
note_fr: Des queues d'écrevisses décortiquées, liées d'une sauce à la crème montée au beurre d'écrevisse et gratinées au plat, maintenue à la carte de l'Auberge du Père Bise par ses successeurs.
why_en: The pigments and aroma compounds of the crayfish shells are fat-soluble, so pounding them into butter and reducing them with cream extracts what water alone leaves in the shell, and the resulting fat-rich sauce browns under the grill instead of splitting.
why_fr: Les pigments et les composés aromatiques des carapaces d'écrevisse sont liposolubles : les piler dans le beurre et les réduire avec la crème extrait ce que l'eau seule laisse dans la carapace, et la sauce grasse ainsi obtenue gratine sous la salamandre au lieu de trancher.
source_quote: Lorsqu'il reprend l'Auberge du Père Bise, Jean Sulpice choisit de préserver le plat emblématique de Marguerite Bise : le gratin de queue d'écrevisses.

audit.problem: Quote is verbatim on the Gault&Millau page and names the dish as the emblematic plate of MARGUERITE Bise specifically — not of "Père Bise" or François Bise. chef_id "bise" is ambiguous and, if it resolves to the male Bise, this is a misattribution. Second risk: produits-laitiers.com presents "le gratin de queues d'écrevisses de Fernand Point" as Point's own famous dish at La Pyramide, so the atlas may end up printing one plate as two different chefs' signature. The sauce detail in note_en (crayfish butter, shallot, white wine, browned in the dish) is not in the cited page.
audit.correction: Set chef_id and note_en to Marguerite Bise explicitly, add a line acknowledging the Fernand Point gratin as the parallel classic, and source the sauce composition separately.

dish_name_fr: Pigeon Prince Rainier III
note_en: A pigeon boned through the back, stuffed with foie gras and black truffle, reshaped into the form of the bird, cooked slowly in a covered pot and carved at the table.
note_fr: Un pigeon désossé par le dos, farci de foie gras et de truffe noire, reconstitué en forme d'oiseau, cuit doucement en cocotte et découpé devant le client.
why_en: Boning removes the skeleton that makes the bird cook at two different rates, so breast and stuffing reach temperature together, while the foie gras melts inside the closed cavity and bastes the lean breast meat from within instead of from the surface.
why_fr: Le désossage supprime la carcasse qui fait cuire l'oiseau à deux vitesses, si bien que le blanc et la farce montent en température ensemble, tandis que le foie gras fond dans la cavité fermée et arrose la chair maigre du blanc par l'intérieur plutôt que par la surface.
source_quote: Raymond Olivier, qui deviendra, avec sa barbe fameuse, la première star culinaire de la télévision française, y règne durant 36 ans, promouvant l'œuf au plat -et foie gras – Louis Oliver, le pigeon farci de ses abats dit Véfour puis Prince Rainier

audit.problem: Quote is verbatim (the page does spell it "Raymond Olivier" in that sentence) and does attach the pigeon called "Véfour puis Prince Rainier" to Oliver at the Grand Véfour. But the same sentence says the pigeon is "farci de ses abats" — stuffed with its own offal — which CONTRADICTS the entry's foie gras and black truffle stuffing. Boning through the back, reshaping the bird, and carving at the table appear nowhere on the page, and why_en's mechanism (foie gras melting and basting from within) is built on the ingredient the source denies.
audit.correction: Either rewrite the entry to the offal stuffing this page carries, or keep the foie gras/truffle version and cite a source that documents it; the Pudlowski blog cannot support both.

reason_if_not_found: No single dish is documented as Jiro Ono's signature. Sukiyabashi Jiro serves only a daily omakase of roughly twenty pieces of nigiri, all of them classic edomae items (akami, kohada, anago, tamagoyaki) that every edomae sushiya serves; the pages opened attribute to him a method and a standard of craft, not a named plate. The Tokyo Metropolitan Government's own article on the restaurant names dishes served there but identifies none as his. The tamagoyaki is widely discussed because of the ten-year apprenticeship shown in 'Jiro Dreams of Sushi', but it is a traditional preparation he did not create, so promoting it to a signature would be an invention. Sources opened: en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php extracts for 'Jiro Ono' and 'Sukiyabashi Jiro'; https://www.tokyoupdates.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/en/post-1581/ ; https://reportergourmet.com/en/chef/839-jiro-ono

dish_name_en: Zucchini flower stuffed with black truffle (le poupeton)
dish_name_fr: Poupeton de fleur de courgette aux truffes noires
note_en: A male zucchini flower stuffed with black truffle and mushrooms, gently cooked and served with a butter sauce built on mushroom fumet; the name comes from the bundled flower's resemblance to a doll.
note_fr: Une fleur de courgette mâle farcie de truffe noire et de champignons, cuite doucement et servie avec un beurre au fumet de champignons ; le nom vient de la ressemblance de la fleur ficelée avec une poupée.
why_en: Truffle aroma compounds are fat-soluble, so the mushroom-fumet butter dissolves them and carries them through the flower's thin, almost tasteless petal wall, which survives the cooking because the flower steams in its own moisture rather than meeting direct heat.
why_fr: Les composés aromatiques de la truffe sont liposolubles : le beurre au fumet de champignons les dissout et les fait passer à travers la paroi mince et presque insipide de la fleur, qui résiste à la cuisson parce qu'elle s'étuve dans sa propre humidité au lieu d'affronter la chaleur directe.
source_quote: Au Moulin de Mougins, Roger Vergé régalait avec sa recette de poupeton (à cause de sa ressemblance avec une poupée) de fleur de courgette (mâle) aux truffes noires du Vaucluse et beurre au fumet de champignons.

audit.problem: Quote is verbatim and attributes the poupeton to Roger Vergé at the Moulin de Mougins, including the doll etymology. One overreach: the page puts only black truffles in the flower ("fleur de courgette (mâle) aux truffes noires du Vaucluse") and the mushrooms in the accompanying butter ("beurre au fumet de champignons"); note_en and the ingredient list move mushrooms into the stuffing. why_en's "steams in its own moisture" is also an inference, not a method the page states.
audit.correction: Move mushrooms out of the stuffing and label them as the fumet for the butter; mark the cooking method as ASSUMED until a recipe source is cited.

dish_name_fr: Biscuit soufflé au chocolat
note_en: A chocolate soufflé biscuit Gagnaire adapted from the soufflé omelette in the Escoffier guide, and the only dish that has stayed on his menu since 1981.
note_fr: Un biscuit soufflé au chocolat que Gagnaire a tiré de l'omelette soufflée du guide Escoffier, et le seul plat resté à sa carte depuis 1981.
why_en: The beaten whites hold air bubbles whose water turns to steam in the oven and inflates the batter, while the egg proteins coagulate and the cocoa butter re-sets on cooling, fixing the foam in place.
why_fr: Les blancs montés emprisonnent des bulles d'air dont l'eau se vaporise au four et fait gonfler l'appareil, tandis que les protéines de l'œuf coagulent et que le beurre de cacao refige en refroidissant, ce qui fixe la mousse.
source_quote: C’est là qu’il tombe sur la recette de l’omelette soufflée, qu’il transformera en biscuit soufflé au chocolat. […] « C’est le seul plat qui reste à la carte depuis 1981. Il évolue un peu mais il est d’une simplicité absolue et les gens aiment bien. »

audit.problem: Both halves of the quote are verbatim, and 1981 is carried by the chef's own words. Two framing issues: the page dates the dish to being ON THE MENU since 1981, not created in 1981; and the same page states "Pierre Gagnaire refuse le concept de « plat signature »", which sits badly against kind: "signature". The page's heading calls it "le soufflé au chocolat" / his madeleine de Proust; "biscuit soufflé au chocolat" is supported by the body text.
audit.correction: Label the year "on the menu since 1981" rather than a creation date, and either change kind or add a line noting Gagnaire rejects the signature-dish framing.

dish_name_en: Louis XV, chocolate and praline crisp
dish_name_fr: Le Louis XV au croustillant de pralin
note_en: A chocolate dessert built on a hazelnut dacquoise and a praline-feuilletine crisp under chocolate mousse and a dark chocolate finish, named after his Monte-Carlo restaurant.
note_fr: Un dessert au chocolat monté sur une dacquoise aux noisettes et un croustillant praliné-feuilletine, surmonté d'une mousse au chocolat et d'une finition chocolat noir, qui porte le nom de son restaurant de Monte-Carlo.
why_en: The praline and crushed crêpe flakes are bound with melted white couverture, and that cocoa butter re-hardens into a fat film around each flake, blocking moisture from the mousse above so the layer stays crisp.
why_fr: Le praliné et la feuilletine sont liés au chocolat de couverture ivoire fondu : en refigeant, ce beurre de cacao enrobe chaque brisure d'un film gras qui bloque l'humidité de la mousse posée dessus, et la couche reste croustillante.
source_quote: The Louis XV is the iconic signature dish of Alain Ducasse’s three-star Michelin restaurant in Monte-Carlo.

audit.problem: Quote is verbatim but the source is a UK retailer's recipe post (Sous Chef, by Nicola Lando, 2013) selling the ingredients alongside it, and its sentence attributes the dish to the RESTAURANT — "the iconic signature dish of Alain Ducasse's three-star Michelin restaurant in Monte-Carlo" — not to a plate Ducasse authored. Every composition detail in the entry (dacquoise, praline-feuilletine with 40g white chocolate couverture, mousse, dark glaze) comes from that shop's own reconstruction, so why_en's white-couverture moisture-barrier mechanism is grounded in the blogger's recipe rather than the house one. The page also gives no year and no creator.
audit.correction: Re-source to Ducasse's own restaurant or publications (the dessert is normally dated to Le Louis XV's opening, 1987, and credited to Ducasse with his pastry chef), and attribute the recipe steps to whoever wrote them.

dish_name_fr: Kir breton
note_en: An edible version of the Breton aperitif served as the first bite at Atelier Crenn: a thin white chocolate and cocoa butter sphere filled with apple cider and topped with crème de cassis.
note_fr: Une version comestible de l'apéritif breton servie en première bouchée à l'Atelier Crenn : une fine sphère de chocolat blanc et de beurre de cacao remplie de cidre et coiffée de crème de cassis.
why_en: Cocoa butter melts just below body temperature, so the shell gives way on the tongue instead of being chewed and releases the cider it held as liquid in a single burst.
why_fr: Le beurre de cacao fond juste en dessous de la température du corps : la coque cède sur la langue au lieu d'être mâchée et libère d'un coup le cidre resté liquide à l'intérieur.
source_quote: One prime example is Crenn's signature dish, Kir Breton. A surprising play on the traditional Kir aperitif of Crenn's beloved Brittany, it is made with a white chocolate shell topped with creme de cassis, which bursts upon eating to reveal an apple cider filling.

audit.problem: Cited URL 301-redirects to www.the50.com; the quote is verbatim there. Two note details are not on the page: cocoa butter (the page says only 'white chocolate shell') and 'served as the first bite at Atelier Crenn'. No year claimed, no superlative in note_en.
audit.correction: Update source_url to https://www.the50.com/northamerica/en/the-list/atelier-crenn.html. Either drop cocoa butter and the 'first bite' claim or add a source that carries them.

dish_name_en: Lobster with tandoori spices, carrot, citrus and coriander
dish_name_fr: Homard aux épices tandoori, mousseline de carottes aux agrumes et coriandre fraîche
note_en: Lobster poached and glazed in a butter sauce spiked with tandoori spices, set against a carrot and candied-citrus purée with fresh coriander; it began as a scallop dish Darroze built after a trip to India and has stayed on the Connaught menu in some form for years.
note_fr: Un homard poché puis glacé dans un beurre relevé d'épices tandoori, accompagné d'une mousseline de carottes aux agrumes confits et de coriandre fraîche ; née d'une version à la Saint-Jacques conçue après un voyage en Inde, la recette figure à la carte du Connaught depuis des années.
why_en: The aroma compounds of the tandoori blend are fat-soluble, so infusing them into the butter sauce fixes them onto the lean lobster meat, while the acid of the citrus stops the carrot purée's sugar from flattening the shellfish's own sweetness.
why_fr: Les composés aromatiques du mélange tandoori étant liposolubles, leur infusion dans le beurre de la sauce les fixe sur la chair maigre du homard, tandis que l'acidité des agrumes empêche le sucre de la mousseline de carotte d'écraser la douceur propre du crustacé.
source_quote: The Tandoori lobster with carrot, citrus, and coriander is one of Hélène’s signature dishes and one of the experience’s highlights from a client perspective.

audit.problem: Quote is verbatim and names the dish as her signature. But the page carries only that one sentence: nothing about poaching, a tandoori butter sauce, a candied-citrus carrot puree, an origin as a scallop dish after a trip to India, or the dish staying on the Connaught menu for years. All of note_en beyond the dish name is unsourced. The page is a promotional guide entry, not editorial reporting. No superlative in note_en.
audit.correction: Cut note_en back to what the source carries, or cite a second source for the preparation and the India/scallop origin.

dish_name_en: Lamb heart tartare with blood sauce and an organ donor card
dish_name_fr: Tartare de cœur d'agneau, sauce sang en poche de transfusion, carte de donneur d'organes
note_en: Raw lamb heart cut as tartare and served in the opened heart, with a cherry-juice and chicken-stock reduction poured over it from a blood transfusion bag and an organ donor registration card set beside the plate; about 1,500 diners went on to register as donors.
note_fr: Un cœur d'agneau cru taillé en tartare et servi dans le cœur ouvert, arrosé d'une réduction de jus de cerise et de fond de volaille versée depuis une poche de transfusion, une carte de donneur d'organes posée à côté ; environ 1 500 convives se sont ensuite inscrits comme donneurs.
why_en: Heart is a lean, hard-working muscle whose high myoglobin content reads as metallic iron on the palate, so the acid and sugar of the cherry reduction mask those iron notes while the gelatine in the chicken stock gives the raw dice the lubrication its low fat content cannot.
why_fr: Le cœur est un muscle maigre et très sollicité dont la forte teneur en myoglobine donne un goût de fer métallique : l'acidité et le sucre de la réduction de cerise masquent ces notes ferreuses, tandis que la gélatine du fond de volaille apporte au tartare cru l'onctuosité que sa maigreur lui refuse.
source_quote: That dish in the middle of his dinner-meets-performance-art menu led to 1,500 people who dined in this tiny Copenhagen restaurant to become organ donors.

audit.problem: Quote is verbatim; the surrounding paragraphs confirm Munk, the lamb heart, the transfusion bag, the cherry-juice-and-chicken-stock reduction and the organ donor card. Two gaps: the page never names the dish (dish_name_en is invented descriptive prose, not a plate name) and never calls it a signature, so kind='signature' is the auditor's inference. 'Served in the opened heart' is also not stated - the page says the heart arrived and the liquid was doused over it.
audit.correction: Either use the plate's real Alchemist name from a source that gives one, or mark kind as 'notable dish' rather than 'signature'. Drop 'served in the opened heart'.

dish_name_en: Caviar with cauliflower cream, double cream and walnut oil
dish_name_fr: Caviar, crème de chou-fleur, crème double et huile de noix
note_en: Caviar served over a cauliflower purée under a lightly salted double cream and finished with walnut oil, one of the plates Jordnær is identified with.
note_fr: Du caviar servi sur une purée de chou-fleur, sous une crème double légèrement salée et terminé à l'huile de noix, l'une des assiettes auxquelles Jordnær est identifié.
why_en: The butterfat of the double cream coats the tongue and dissolves the fat-soluble aroma of the walnut oil, so the salt released when the roe membranes burst is buffered and spreads slowly instead of spiking.
why_fr: La matière grasse de la crème double tapisse la langue et dissout les arômes liposolubles de l'huile de noix, si bien que le sel libéré à l'éclatement des membranes des œufs est tamponné et se diffuse lentement au lieu de saturer d'un coup.
source_quote:
Caviar, cauliflower cream, and walnut oil
A signature dish at Jordnær!

audit.problem: The source_quote stitches two SEPARATE figcaptions on two different gallery images: 'Caviar, cauliflower cream, and walnut oil' captions image -2019-13.jpg, and 'A signature dish at Jordnaer!' captions image -2019-12.jpg. The page contains no sentence tying the word signature to this dish; the link is positional inference. Separately, 'double cream' appears nowhere on the page (0 occurrences) yet sits in dish_name_en, dish_name_fr, the ingredient list and note_en, and it is the component why_en's whole mechanism rests on. The dish is real - other sources describe caviar with cauliflower, double cream and walnut oil as a Jordnaer signature - but this page does not carry it.
audit.correction: Replace the source with one that states the dish and its double cream in prose, or drop double cream from the name, ingredients, note and mechanism and keep the source as a photo-caption citation only.

dish_name_fr: Brochette Margaridou
note_en: A breaded and deep-fried skewer of veal sweetbread, Auvergne dry-cured ham and morels, adapted from the notebooks of the Auvergne cook Margaridou, first served as one of the garnishes of the plate that won Marcon the 1995 Bocuse d'Or and kept on the restaurant's menu ever since.
note_fr: Brochette panée puis frite de ris de veau, jambon sec d'Auvergne et morilles, adaptée des carnets de la cuisinière auvergnate Margaridou, servie d'abord comme l'une des garnitures du plat qui a valu à Marcon le Bocuse d'Or 1995 et restée à la carte du restaurant depuis.
why_en: The chilled mushroom-roux panade packed around the sweetbread and morels is a starch gel that binds their water, so the breadcrumb crust colours and sets in the 160 °C fat before the interior can dry out.
why_fr: La panade de roux aux champignons figée autour du ris de veau et des morilles est un gel d'amidon qui retient leur eau : la panure se colore et se fige dans la friture à 160 °C avant que l'intérieur ne se dessèche.
source_quote: Un plat signature ? La brochette Margaridou, qui représente le Bocuse d'or pour moi. Évidemment, les champignons sont le cœur de ma cuisine.

audit.problem: Quote is verbatim (curly apostrophes on the page) and Marcon names the brochette Margaridou as his plat signature. But the string '1995' does not appear anywhere on the page - the year was imported from outside. It happens to be correct (Marcon won the Bocuse d'Or on 26 January 1995), so this is an uncited fact rather than a wrong one. The page also carries none of the composition: no sweetbread, morels, ham, breadcrumbs, truffle, no Margaridou notebooks, no 'one of the garnishes of the Bocuse d'Or plate', no 'kept on the menu ever since'.
audit.correction: Set year to '—' for this source, or add a second citation for 1995 and the ingredients (bocusedor-winners.com / saga-bocusedor.com carry the year; academiedugout.fr carries the recipe). Also check black truffle - it is not in the commonly published ingredient list.

dish_name_fr: Biscuit de brochet et lotte du lac, bouillon d'oignon
dish_name_en: Pike and lake burbot biscuit in onion broth
note_en: Pike and lake burbot flesh whipped with cream and eggs into a light baked mousse, served in a shallow bowl under a bread tuile with a grilled-onion broth and mountain herbs.
note_fr: Chair de brochet et de lotte du lac montée à la crème et aux œufs en une mousse légère cuite au four, servie en assiette creuse sous une tuile de pain avec un bouillon d'oignon grillé et des plantes de montagne.
why_en: Salting and blending the pike releases its myosin, which emulsifies the cream and traps air, and gentle baking coagulates that protein network around the water and fat so the foam holds its shape without gelatine.
why_fr: Le sel et le broyage libèrent la myosine de la chair de brochet, qui émulsionne la crème et emprisonne l'air ; la cuisson douce coagule ce réseau de protéines autour de l'eau et du gras, si bien que la mousse tient sans gélatine.
source_quote: Si vous deviez choisir un plat emblème de votre carrière, lequel choisiriez-vous ? La Lotte du lac et brochet en biscuit, bouillon d'oignon achillée et lierre terrestre... c'est un plat qui réunit les produits que j'aime travailler : les poissons du lac et les plantes de montagne.

audit.problem: The quote is accurate (the ellipsis stands in for 'parce que') and Renaut names this as the plat embleme of his career, so attribution holds. But note_en and why_en contradict the recipe printed on the same page. The page says the farce is steamed - 'faites cuire a la vapeur 15 min' - not baked, so why_en's 'gentle baking coagulates that protein network' misstates the method the source gives. The page also says 'Posez la farce sur le pain': the mousse sits ON a slice of pain de mie which is then coloured in clarified butter, not 'under a bread tuile'. The recipe further lists crayfish bisque, sugar, tapioca pearls and fritters, none of which reach the ingredient list.
audit.correction: Change 'baked' to 'steamed' in note_en/why_en (the myosin mechanism survives the correction), replace 'under a bread tuile' with the bread base the recipe describes, and add crayfish bisque to the ingredients.

dish_name_fr: Timbale de pomme et foie gras à l'huile de vanille
dish_name_en: Apple and foie gras timbale with vanilla oil
note_en: Alternating layers of caramelised apple and duck foie gras pressed into a timbale and dressed with vanilla-infused oil, on El Celler de Can Roca's menu since 1996 and formally given to the city of Girona in 2009.
note_fr: Couches alternées de pomme caramélisée et de foie gras de canard pressées en timbale et nappées d'une huile infusée à la vanille, à la carte d'El Celler de Can Roca depuis 1996 et offerte à la ville de Gérone en 2009.
why_en: The malic acid of the caramelised apple cuts the fat film the foie gras leaves on the palate, while vanillin, being fat-soluble, dissolves into that same fat and carries its aroma through every layer.
why_fr: L'acide malique de la pomme caramélisée coupe le film gras que le foie gras laisse en bouche, tandis que la vanilline, liposoluble, se dissout dans cette même graisse et en diffuse l'arôme à chaque couche.
source_quote: Una muestra es uno de los platos esenciales de la cocina de El Celler: Timbal de manzana y foigras al aceite de vainilla. Un plato histórico de los Roca y que años más tarde, en 2009, se donó a la ciudad de Girona en el Pregó de Fires.

audit.problem: Quote is verbatim and sits under the 1996 heading of the official timeline, so both 1996 and the 2009 donation to Girona at the Prego de Fires are supported. Two smaller issues: the page describes neither the construction (alternating caramelised apple layers, duck foie gras) nor 'on the menu since 1996' - it says only 'plato historico' and 'uno de los platos esenciales', and the 1996 entry is hedged as 'En estos anos'. The page also writes 'foigras' without specifying duck, and credits 'los Roca' collectively rather than a named chef.
audit.correction: Soften 'on the menu since 1996' to 'dates from 1996', and source the layered construction and the duck separately, or drop those specifics. No superlative in note_en.

dish_name_en: Razor clams, minerals and sour cream
dish_name_fr: Couteaux, minéraux et crème aigre
note_en: A tartare of diced razor clam bound with crème fraîche and lemon, served inside an edible baked dough 'shell' painted with charcoal and algae powder to look like the real one.
note_fr: Un tartare de couteaux en dés lié à la crème fraîche et au citron, servi dans une fausse coquille de pâte cuite, peinte au charbon et à la poudre d'algues.
why_en: The lemon juice and zest denature the proteins of the raw diced clam so the flesh firms without any heat, while the fat of the 38% crème fraîche coats the dice and slows the acid's action on them.
why_fr: Le jus et le zeste de citron dénaturent les protéines de la chair crue de couteau, qui raffermit sans cuisson, tandis que la matière grasse de la crème fraîche à 38 % enrobe les dés et freine l'action de l'acide sur eux.
source_quote: Known for toying with diners’ expectations of the norm, many of his dishes are not as they first seem and his Razor Clams, Minerals and Sour Cream is a case in point.

audit.problem: None. Page loads; the quoted sentence is present verbatim, including the opening clause 'Known for toying with diners' expectations of the norm'. The page attributes the dish to Rasmus Kofoed of Geranium and calls his dishes signature dishes. Year is '—', which is fine (the page's 2019 date is a publication date, not a creation date). Every listed ingredient is in the published recipe: 'creme fraiche (38% fat)', '10g charcoal powder', '10g algae powder', lemon zest and juice, '8g chopped parsley', '2 thin wheat dough sheets' for the edible shell — so the 38% figure in why_en is source-backed, not invented. why_en is causal (acid denatures protein, fat coats and slows acid contact), not praise. No superlative in note_en.

dish_name_fr: Pâtes disparaissantes
note_en: Noodles made with no flour and no egg — strips of melted Beaufort set firm — that dissolve into the broth poured over them at the table.
note_fr: Des pâtes sans farine ni œuf — des lamelles de beaufort fondu puis figées — qui se dissolvent dans le bouillon versé à table.
why_en: The noodle is pure cheese and holds its shape only while cold: the hot broth takes it past the melting point of the milk fat, the casein network slackens, and the strip collapses into the liquid, which it salts and enriches as it goes.
why_fr: La pâte n'est que du fromage et ne tient sa forme qu'à froid : le bouillon chaud lui fait dépasser le point de fusion de la matière grasse, le réseau de caséine se relâche et la lamelle s'effondre dans le liquide, qu'elle sale et enrichit en disparaissant.
source_quote: Et le bon vieux tour des pâtes disparaissantes (beaufort et safran en lamelles qui s’évanouissent dans un bouillon de champignons) fait toujours son petit effet de surprise pour les novices, se révélant véritablement délicieux pour les vieux « fans » du maître – dont nous sommes -.

audit.problem: None. Page loads; the quoted sentence is present verbatim with beaufort, safran and bouillon de champignons. 'Le bon vieux tour des pâtes disparaissantes' plus 'du maître' ties the dish to Veyrat's own repertoire, not to a house style. Year '—' is correct: the page dates nothing. why_en is a mechanism (fat past melting point, casein network slackens). No superlative in note_en. Residual: 'no flour and no egg' is an inference from 'beaufort et safran en lamelles' rather than a stated fact, but it is the only reading the quote allows.

dish_name_en: Crisp langoustine tart under oscietra caviar
dish_name_fr: Tarte friande de langoustine recouverte de grains de caviar Osciètre
note_en: A thin crisp pastry tart of langoustine finished with a layer of oscietra caviar spread over it with a spatula.
note_fr: Une tarte fine et croustillante à la langoustine, recouverte d'une couche de grains de caviar Osciètre étalée à la spatule.
why_en: The salt of the dish comes from the caviar's own brine, released as the grains burst on the palate and seasoning the langoustine from above, while the baked pastry underneath stays dry and supplies the only crisp texture against two soft layers.
why_fr: Le sel du plat vient de la saumure du caviar, libérée quand les grains éclatent en bouche et qui assaisonne la langoustine par le dessus, tandis que la pâte cuite en dessous reste sèche et apporte la seule texture croustillante face à deux couches molles.
source_quote: Parmi ses plats emblématiques figurent par exemple le ris de veau en noix croustillante ou encore sa tarte friande de langoustine recouverte de grains de caviar Osciètre.

audit.problem: None. Page loads; the quoted sentence is present verbatim and 'Parmi ses plats emblématiques' carries the claim that this is Alléno's own named plate, not a restaurant style. No year on the page, and the record says '—'. why_en is a mechanism (brine released on burst seasons from above; baked pastry stays dry and supplies the sole crisp layer). No superlative in note_en.

dish_name_fr: Sardine, velours d'Eden
note_en: A grilled sardine served with the velours d'Eden, an emulsified sauce scented with fennel and marigold that grew out of a vitello tonnato Donckele had failed and reworked.
note_fr: Une sardine grillée servie avec le velours d'Eden, sauce émulsionnée marquée par le fenouil et la tagète, née d'une sauce vitello tonnato ratée puis retravaillée par Donckele.
why_en: Sardine flesh is oily, and the bonito and Lambrusco vinegars make the velours acidic enough to cut that fat on the palate, while the emulsified olive oil keeps the sauce clinging to the fish instead of running off it.
why_fr: La chair de la sardine est grasse : les vinaigres de bonite et de Lambrusco rendent le velours assez acide pour trancher ce gras en bouche, tandis que l'huile d'olive émulsionnée fait tenir la sauce sur le poisson au lieu de la laisser couler.
source_quote: C'est un plat signature, fondateur, presque un manifeste.

audit.problem: The dish is real and is Donckele's — the page's section is headed 'Sardine, velours d'Eden : un hasard devenu une signature' and confirms the failed 'sauce vitello tonnato ratée' origin. But the cited sentence, 'C'est un plat signature, fondateur, presque un manifeste.', names neither the dish nor the chef; it carries the claim only by sitting under that heading, so it cannot stand as the quote. Worse, the ingredient list and the entire why_en rest on specifics the page does not contain. The page gives the sauce only as 'une sauce fraîche, addictive, anisée, marquée par la tagète, le fenouil, la Provence' — no vinegar of any kind, no olive oil, no tarragon. So 'bonito vinegar' and the 'bonite et Lambrusco' vinegars that why_en makes load-bearing are unsourced, and 'tarragon' appears on the page only in a different dish ('lapin à la moutarde et à l'estragon'), which is where it seems to have been borrowed from. The page also never says the sardine is grilled.
audit.correction: Replace the source_quote with the section heading sentence that names the dish, or with 'La sardine, c'est le poisson que je préfère en termes de puissance et de goût'. Cut 'bonito vinegar' and 'tarragon' from ingredients, or cite a source that states them. Drop 'grilled' from note_en. Rewrite why_en on what the page supports — the anise of fennel and the tagète against an oily flesh, and the emulsion's cling — instead of on two vinegars the source never mentions.

dish_name_en: Langoustine sorta with rice noodles and foie gras mayonnaise
dish_name_fr: Sorta de langoustines, vermicelles de riz et mayonnaise de foie gras
note_en: Langoustines bound in a sheaf of rice noodles with a foie gras mayonnaise, the first major dish Elena Arzak created at her family's restaurant, at the age of 25.
note_fr: Des langoustines liées en gerbe de vermicelles de riz avec une mayonnaise de foie gras — la « sorta de cigalas » —, premier grand plat créé par Elena Arzak, à 25 ans.
why_en: The egg-yolk lecithin in the mayonnaise holds the foie gras fat dispersed as fine droplets, so the sauce coats the langoustine as a stable cream instead of splitting into grease.
why_fr: La lécithine du jaune d'œuf maintient la graisse du foie gras dispersée en fines gouttelettes, si bien que la sauce nappe la langoustine en crème stable au lieu de trancher en gras.
source_quote: Es el primer gran plato de Elena Arzak, que contaba por entonces con 25 años.

audit.problem: Wrong-chef risk, and a dead URL. The cited saberysabor.com URL 301-redirects to https://www.hellochefs.es/alta-cocina/v/siete-claves-y-siete-platos-para-entender-un-mito; the content is there and the quote 'Es el primer gran plato de Elena Arzak, que contaba por entonces con 25 años.' is present verbatim, the dish is 'Sorta de cigalas y fideos de arroz con mayonesa de foie', and 1996 is on the page. The defect is the key: the source pins this dish to ELENA Arzak specifically, while chef_id is the bare 'arzak', which in any atlas resolves to Juan Mari. note_en says Elena, so the record contradicts its own key. For a cookery-school atlas that is a misattribution waiting to happen. why_en is a mechanism (yolk lecithin holds the foie fat as a dispersed emulsion). 'First major dish' is not an editorial superlative — it is the source's own 'primer gran plato'.
audit.correction: Set chef_id to 'elena_arzak' (or whatever key the atlas uses for Elena) and keep Juan Mari's entry separate; if the atlas has only one Arzak seat, the dish does not belong in it. Update source_url to the hellochefs.es address, since the cited one no longer serves the page.

reason_if_not_found: No opened source names a single dish as Ana Roš's signature, and the one source that addresses the question directly records her rejecting the concept: in a Stone Journal interview she explains why she does not believe in signature dishes and calls them irrelevant, since the menu at Hiša Franko is rebuilt around whatever the Soča valley yields that season. Her English Wikipedia entry names no dish at all. What is documented is signature INGREDIENTS — marble trout above all, which has never been off the menu — not a named plate. Candidates circulating in search-engine summaries (a corn beignet, a raw marble trout salad) did not survive opening the pages: neither the Food Perestroika account of the beignet nor the Accounting For Taste review contains the word 'signature' anywhere, so that framing came from the summariser, not from any source. Promoting either would be attributing a menu item, not a documented signature.
source_quote: It's an important example of why I don't believe in signature dishes.

dish_name_fr: Pain perdu « Grand Tradition 2008 »
note_en: A small block of fried brioche hollowed out and filled with caramelised onion, topped with aged Vacche Rosse cheese, black truffle and a few drops of long-aged vinegar, finished at the table.
note_fr: Un petit pavé de brioche frite, évidé et garni d'oignon caramélisé, recouvert de Parmigiano Reggiano Vacche Rosse, de truffe noire et de quelques gouttes de vinaigre longuement vieilli, terminé devant le client.
why_en: The truffle's aroma compounds are fat-soluble, so the warm cheese fat and the butter in the fried brioche dissolve and release them, while the acetic acid of the aged vinegar cuts that same fat.
why_fr: Les composés aromatiques de la truffe sont liposolubles : la graisse du fromage chaud et le beurre de la brioche frite les dissolvent et les libèrent, tandis que l'acide acétique du vinaigre vieilli tranche cette même graisse.
source_quote: Signature French toast "grand tradition 2008" with black truffle, Parmigiano Reggiano Vacche Rosse cheese & vinegar aged on juniper wood

audit.problem: Attribution, year and signature status are clean — the caption is present verbatim, says 'Signature', and 2008 is inside the dish's own name. But note_en describes a preparation the page contradicts. The page's paragraph reads: 'A toast soaked in butter with a Maillard crust. Tableside, it is topped with a cream made from the finest Parmigiano Reggiano Vacche Rosse, a few drops of vinegar aged on juniper wood, and a sinful amount of black truffle...'. That is a buttered toast topped with a cheese CREAM — not a block 'hollowed out and filled with caramelised onion'. Onion appears nowhere on the page. And the record's 'aged balsamic vinegar' is contradicted by the very sentence it cites, which says vinegar aged on juniper wood. The page's own superlative ('most famous of all Frantzén's dishes') was correctly kept out of note_en.
audit.correction: Change the ingredient to 'vinegar aged on juniper wood' and drop 'balsamic'. Either remove the hollowed-block-and-caramelised-onion description in favour of the source's buttered toast with Vacche Rosse cream, truffle and a few drops of vinegar finished tableside, or cite a second source that documents the onion filling.

dish_name_fr: Bao au stilton et cerises amarena
note_en: A steamed wheat bun filled with melted Stilton and amarena cherries, served as the cheese stage of her tasting menu at Yam'Tcha.
note_fr: Une brioche vapeur farcie de stilton fondu et de cerises amarena, servie comme étape fromage de son menu dégustation chez Yam'Tcha.
why_en: Steaming holds the bun at boiling point in saturated vapour, so the crumb stays moist and the Stilton melts to a smooth liquid instead of splitting, while the acidity and sugar of the amarena syrup offset the salt and the sharp fatty acids of the blue cheese.
why_fr: La cuisson vapeur maintient le pain à 100 °C dans une atmosphère saturée : la mie reste humide et le stilton fond en une masse lisse au lieu de trancher, tandis que l'acidité et le sucre du sirop d'amarena compensent le sel et les acides gras piquants du bleu.
source_quote: On enchaine avec le plat signature d'Adeline Grattard, le bao Stilton Amarena.

audit.problem: The quote is present verbatim — 'On enchaine avec le plat signature d'Adeline Grattard, le bao Stilton Amarena.' — and the page confirms the Stilton-and-amarena pairing and the signature status, so dish and chef are solid. The service context in note_en is not. The article is about the Yam'Tcha takeaway counter ('comptoir spécialisé dans la vente à emporter', 4 rue Sauval), where the baos are sold over the counter; nothing on the page places this bao as the cheese stage of a tasting menu. note_en states that as fact. why_en is a mechanism (saturated vapour at boiling point keeps the crumb moist and the blue melting smooth; amarena acid and sugar offset salt and short-chain fatty acids). No superlative. Year '—' is right.
audit.correction: Drop 'served as the cheese stage of her tasting menu at Yam'Tcha' unless a restaurant-menu source is added; the cited page supports only that it is her signature bao, sold at the Yam'Tcha boutique counter.

dish_name_en: Tocino del cielo (candied egg yolk on a caramelised macaron)
dish_name_fr: Tocino del cielo (jaune d'œuf confit sur macaron caramélisé)
note_en: An Andalusian dessert of egg yolk set in sugar syrup, served at Le Chateaubriand as a single caramelised bite sitting on a macaron base.
note_fr: Un dessert andalou de jaune d'œuf pris dans un sirop de sucre, servi au Chateaubriand en une seule bouchée caramélisée posée sur un macaron.
why_en: The concentrated sugar syrup binds the free water and raises the temperature at which the yolk's proteins coagulate, so the yolk sets into a dense, smooth custard rather than curdling into grains.
why_fr: Le sirop de sucre très concentré retient l'eau libre et élève la température de coagulation des protéines du jaune, qui prend alors en une crème dense et lisse au lieu de grainer.
source_quote: Hormis le tocino de cielo, on ne parle pas de « plat signature » avec Inaki, c'est d'ailleurs une expression qu'il déteste.

audit.problem: Quote is verbatim on the Konbini page and names tocino de cielo as the one dish Aizpitarte will allow to be called a signature. But the page carries the name only: the plate description in dish_name_en and note_en (single caramelised bite on a macaron base, served at Le Chateaubriand) appears nowhere on it, and neither do the four listed ingredients.
audit.correction: Keep the entry and add a second source for the composition. Gastroeconomy's account of the dessert describes the almond-meringue macaron base and a 24-hour cure in caramel syrup, and puts it on the menu since 2010 — which would also let year move off '—'.

dish_name_fr: Dum biryani d'agneau à la mode de Calcutta
note_en: A Calcutta-style dum biryani of lamb, potato and saffron rice that Asma Khan inherited from her family's cooks and serves to the whole dining room at once at her Sunday biryani supper club.
note_fr: Un dum biryani à la mode de Calcutta, composé d'agneau, de pommes de terre et de riz safrané, hérité des cuisinières de sa famille et servi en même temps à toute la salle lors de son supper club du dimanche.
why_en: The pot is sealed before the slow cooking, so the rice finishes swelling in trapped lamb-and-saffron steam rather than in water, while the potato absorbs the rendered fat that would otherwise pool at the base.
why_fr: La marmite est scellée avant la cuisson lente : le riz achève donc de gonfler dans la vapeur d'agneau et de safran retenue à l'intérieur plutôt que dans l'eau, et la pomme de terre absorbe la graisse fondue qui s'accumulerait sinon au fond.
source_quote: On Sundays Asma hosts a biryani supper club at the restaurant instead of the regular menu, where her signature biryani is unveiled in the dining room and served to everyone at the same time in the traditional 'dawaat' style.

audit.problem: The quote is verbatim on the Great British Chefs page, but it establishes only 'her signature biryani' served dawaat style. Calcutta-style, lamb, potato, saffron, ghee and the provenance claim 'inherited from her family's cooks' are all absent from the page, so the source does not carry the dish as named.
audit.correction: Either rename the entry to what the page supports — a signature biryani unveiled and served to the whole room at the Sunday supper club — or cite a source that names the Calcutta lamb-and-potato version before keeping the current title and ingredient list.

dish_name_fr: Aubergine rôtie, sauce au babeurre
note_en: Roast aubergine halves spooned with a buttermilk and yoghurt sauce and scattered with za'atar and pomegranate seeds, from Ottolenghi's 2010 vegetable book Plenty.
note_fr: Des moitiés d'aubergine rôties, nappées d'une sauce au babeurre et au yaourt et parsemées de za'atar et de graines de grenade, tirées de Plenty (2010), le livre de légumes d'Ottolenghi.
why_en: Roasting collapses the aubergine's air-filled flesh so it drinks up the olive oil, and the lactic acid in the buttermilk and yoghurt cuts that oil on the palate.
why_fr: La cuisson au four fait s'effondrer la chair spongieuse de l'aubergine, qui absorbe alors l'huile d'olive, et l'acide lactique du babeurre et du yaourt vient trancher ce gras en bouche.
source_quote: From Plenty by Yotam Ottolenghi, this simple recipe for roast aubergines with buttermilk sauce is a delight. Featuring signature Ottolenghi ingredients, including aubergine and za'atar, it is a perfect vegetarian main course.

audit.problem: Quote is verbatim and the page carries authorship (an authorised extract from Plenty) plus all six ingredients. Two smaller faults: the page says aubergine and za'atar are 'signature Ottolenghi ingredients', not that this is a signature dish, so kind='signature' leans on a misread; and note_en's '2010' is not on the page, which credits only 'Plenty by Yotam Ottolenghi. (Ebury £26)'.
audit.correction: Set kind to 'memorable', or cite Plenty's publication data for both the signature framing and the 2010 date. The recipe attribution and ingredients need no further sourcing.

dish_name_fr: Dentucky Fried Chicken
note_en: A deboned chicken wing stuffed with glutinous rice and a filling that changes with the season, fried and handed over in a red-and-white striped takeaway box printed with Hasegawa's face.
note_fr: Une aile de poulet désossée, farcie de riz gluant et d'une garniture qui change au fil des saisons, frite puis remise dans une boîte à emporter rayée rouge et blanc à l'effigie de Hasegawa.
why_en: Deboning presses the collagen-rich skin directly against the rice, so in the fryer the skin renders and dries into a crust while the enclosed rice steams in the wing's own moisture and stays soft.
why_fr: Le désossage plaque la peau riche en collagène directement contre le riz : à la friture, la peau fond puis se dessèche en croûte tandis que le riz, enfermé, cuit à la vapeur de l'aile elle-même et reste moelleux.
source_quote: The restaurant's signature Dentucky Fried Chicken is a crispy chicken wing stuffed with flavored sticky rice and served in a red- and white-striped box adorned with Hasegawa's face.

audit.problem: Quote is verbatim on the Newsweek page and carries the dish name, the sticky-rice stuffing and the striped box with Hasegawa's face. It does not carry deboning, the season-changing filling, or green plum, black sesame and pickled daikon — three of the five listed ingredients are unsourced, and why_en's mechanism is built on the unsourced deboning.
audit.correction: Reduce the ingredient list to chicken wing and glutinous rice plus a seasonal filling, or source the three specifics. The same page supplies a usable note_en fact the entry omits: the dish began as a parody of Japan's KFC-at-Christmas custom.

dish_name_fr: Thon en croûte de fourmis culonas
note_en: A loin of tuna seared under a crust of toasted, ground leafcutter ants and served with cane syrup and a pigeon-pea cream; it was among the first uses of a Colombian street-food insect on a fine-dining plate.
note_fr: Un pavé de thon saisi sous une croûte de fourmis culonas grillées et moulues, servi avec du sirop de canne et une crème de pois d'Angole ; ce fut l'un des premiers passages d'un insecte de la rue colombienne à la haute cuisine.
why_en: The ground ants are fatty enough to render and brown into a crust during the sear, while the formic acid they carry cuts the sweetness of the cane syrup.
why_fr: Les fourmis moulues sont assez grasses pour fondre et brunir en croûte pendant la saisie, tandis que l'acide formique qu'elles contiennent tranche la douceur du sirop de canne.
source_quote: Conviven sin afán el atún en costra de hormigas culonas, miel de caña y crema de guandú con una ensalada de tubérculos andinos, hojas de cedrón, caracoles y flores de acedera.

audit.problem: The page opens and the quoted sentence is there, attributing the dish to her restaurant Leo. Three defects follow. Long pepper is not in the source. note_en's 'among the first uses of a Colombian street-food insect on a fine-dining plate' is a priority claim the page never makes. And why_en's chemistry is wrong: hormigas culonas are Atta laevigata, a myrmicine, and formic acid is a formicine venom trait — myrmicine venoms are protein-based, with formic acid not detected in them.
audit.correction: Drop long pepper, delete the priority claim, and rewrite the acid half of why_en. The fat half stands — these ants are fat-rich enough to render and brown — so the crust mechanism survives without the formic-acid sentence.

dish_name_fr: Foie gras et gruau de maïs
note_en: Seared foie gras over slow-cooked corn grits with a red-wine gravy, built from the Southern lunch-counter dish of beef liver and grits.
note_fr: Du foie gras poêlé sur un gruau de maïs cuit lentement, nappé d'une sauce au vin rouge, construit à partir du plat sudiste de foie de bœuf au gruau.
why_en: Fat rendered from the searing foie gras emulsifies into the starch the slow-cooked corn has released, and the acid in the red-wine gravy cuts through that fat.
why_fr: La graisse rendue par le foie gras à la poêle s'émulsionne dans l'amidon libéré par le maïs cuit lentement, et l'acidité de la sauce au vin rouge vient trancher ce gras.
source_quote: Bailey also pulls influence from European cuisine, including in one of her signature dishes: foie gras and grits.

audit.problem: Quote is verbatim on the Wikipedia article and Mashama Bailey is correctly identified as the chef whose signature dish it is. The red-wine gravy and the beef-liver-and-grits lunch-counter origin in note_en are not on the page, and why_en's acid clause depends on that unsourced gravy.
audit.correction: Source the liver-and-grits origin from an interview where Bailey tells it, or trim note_en and why_en to what the page carries — European technique over Southern grits — and drop red wine from the ingredient list until it is sourced.

reason_if_not_found: No single dish is documented as Selassie Atadika's signature. Every source I opened describes a philosophy and a format rather than a named plate: her own Midunu chef page states only "At Midunu, Selassie cooks with curiosity and restraint, allowing ingredients, place, and conversation to lead", and the TIME Earth Awards profile names no dish at all, describing her work through ingredients and sustainability principles. The two plausible candidates both fail. Garifoto is documented by Al Jazeera as her mother's Sunday recipe and her own quarantine comfort food, not a Midunu creation — the piece quotes her saying "In these times of uncertainty and in hopes of finding comfort, I find myself turning to mum's go-to garifoto." The Midunu chocolate truffles are a confectionery product line that grew out of the tasting menu's final course, not a dish. Attributing a signature dish here would mean stretching the New African Cuisine style into a plate that no source names.
source_quote: In these times of uncertainty and in hopes of finding comfort, I find myself turning to mum's go-to garifoto.

dish_name_fr: Champignons shiitake braisés
note_en: Whole shiitake caps braised slowly in soy sauce, perilla oil and rice syrup until the liquid reduces to a glaze, a dish Jeong Kwan first cooked for her father when he came to the temple to take her home.
note_fr: Des chapeaux de shiitake entiers braisés lentement dans la sauce soja, l'huile de périlla et le sirop de riz jusqu'à ce que le liquide se réduise en glaçage, un plat que Jeong Kwan a d'abord cuisiné pour son père venu au temple la ramener à la maison.
why_en: Shiitake carry the nucleotide guanylate, which multiplies the savoury effect of the glutamate in the soy sauce, while the long reduction drives the salted liquid into the porous caps and leaves the rice syrup behind as a clinging glaze.
why_fr: Le shiitake contient du guanylate, un nucléotide qui démultiplie l'effet savoureux du glutamate de la sauce soja, tandis que la longue réduction fait pénétrer le liquide salé dans les chapeaux poreux et laisse le sirop de riz former un glaçage qui nappe les champignons.
source_quote: So ironically, the braised shitake mushrooms have become my signature dish, but I do not eat them anymore.

audit.problem: Quote is verbatim on the Yale page and the father story is close to it (he visited for two weeks, asked her to return home with him, bowed to her after eating, and died a week later). The preparation is not. The page describes mushrooms boiled in a clay pot for three hours and names sesame oil, sesame powder and eight-year-fermented soy sauce; perilla oil and rice syrup appear nowhere, so why_en's reduction of a syrup into a clinging glaze describes a dish the source does not.
audit.correction: Replace perilla oil and rice syrup with sesame oil, sesame powder and aged soy sauce, and rebuild why_en around the three-hour clay-pot braise. The guanylate-and-glutamate synergy is sound and can stay.
